verdicts.quote: Unchecked type assertion in deepSet panics on conflicting deepObject query keys (unauthenticated remote panic)
verdicts.why: No finding describes the advisory's mechanism: sliceMapToSlice reconstructing an array from the intermediate index-keyed map by reading the LARGEST attacker-supplied bracket index and allocating one slot per position from 0 to that index, before schema validation (maxItems) runs, so ?param[items][50000000]=x forces ~6.1 GiB of heap. Nothing in the list mentions sliceMapToSlice, index-driven preallocation, maxItems being applied too late, or memory growth from a query parameter at all. The closest finding is N05 (quoted), which is in the same file and the same deepObject decode path (req_resp_decoder.go, ValidateParameter -> decodeStyledParameter -> DecodeObject -> makeObject) but is a DIFFERENT defect: an unchecked type assertion `m = m[key].(map[string]any)` in deepSet at line 945 that panics when two query keys disagree about the depth of a node ("interface conversion: interface {} is string, not map[string]interface {}"). Its failure mode is an immediate panic on a malformed key path, not unbounded allocation; it fires on conflicting key shapes rather than on a large numeric index; and fixing it (comma-ok assertion) leaves the advisory's allocation entirely intact. Also considered and rejected: N02, which is uncontrolled resource consumption in openapi3filter but from io.ReadAll of request/response bodies and the multipart part loop - proportional to bytes actually sent, i.e. the opposite of the advisory's tiny-request amplification.

verdicts.quote: Rendering a validation error panics when the rejected value is not JSON-encodable.
verdicts.why: No finding covers openapi3filter/validation_error_encoder.go at all: nothing names ConvertErrors, ValidationErrorEncoder or convertParseError, and nothing identifies the nil-pointer dereference `e.Parameter.In == "query"` where e.Parameter is nil for a body-level error, nor the multipart/form-data-specific trigger (a malformed scalar form field such as a non-numeric value for an integer property) versus application/json being unaffected. The closest finding is N12 (quoted), which shares only the outcome - a panic while an error is rendered - but is a different defect: SchemaError.Error() in openapi3/schema.go:3197/3201 calls panic(err) when json.Encoder refuses err.Schema or err.Value, reached via a YAML body decoding to map[any]any. Different package, different function, different mechanism (deliberate panic on an encoder error, not an unchecked nil pointer), different trigger (application/yaml body with a non-string mapping key, not multipart), and a fix to either one does nothing for the other. N05 is also a remote panic but sits in the deepObject query decoder, further away still.
